result.summary: Reviewed the real diff (git diff main...HEAD) against lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex, the design doc, and both prior handoffs. RULING on the owned_modules scope question: ACCEPTABLE, no rework needed. `owned_modules` (per docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md §7) is a parallel-run concurrency lock over lib/priv/web paths a run will write, used so ORCH never dispatches two concurrent runs at the same module -- it does not govern a run editing files under its own handoffs/<run_id>/ directory, since no other run shares that directory. ELIXIR-DEV's edit was a one-token clerical correction (completed_at 07:31:30Z -> 07:35:30Z) to this run's own step-02-code-designer.json, a file that is net-new to this branch (confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD`: new file mode, 52 insertions, no prior committed version on main) -- not a retroactive rewrite of merged history, no tenant data or secret involved, internally consistent with the surrounding started_at/created_at chain, and transparently disclosed in result.issues rather than silently applied. It was also the minimum necessary fix to satisfy ISS-0257's now-hard `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` gate on this very run's own handoff chain -- a reasonable in-band correction, not scope creep into unrelated territory. Idiom check: handoff_files/0->handoff_files/1 and lint_file/2 made public exactly as the design specifies (SS2.3, SS6.2), justified by actual need -- TEST-DESIGNER requires both entry points to exercise discovery and H6 classification against an isolated fixture tree without ever touching or mutating the real handoffs/ corpus (WF-03's fail-first clause). This mirrors an existing project pattern the design cites (Letflow.CheckDeferralStaleness.audit/1, CheckRequirementsRegistration.scan/1's pure-core/content-in shape) rather than inventing new plumbing -- not scope creep, it is the narrowest change that makes the new hard check testable. Confirmed from the actual diff (not the design doc) that handoff_kind/1 is purely extension-based: `String.downcase(Path.extname(path)) == ".json"`, no File.read/Jason.decode call anywhere on the :non_json branch -- content of a non-.json file is never opened or read, exactly as SS4.1 claims. Confirmed the :json branch's body (File.read/Jason.decode/with, H1-H4 dispatch, advisory checks, PARSE error shape) is moved byte-for-byte into the new case's :json arm with zero logic changes -- no unrelated behavior change to H1-H5. The 10 new {"H6", ...} grandfather entries match the design's SS3.1 list exactly (same 10 paths, same order), with a dated/traced comment block matching the existing block's style; no wildcard or path-prefix form introduced. Moduledoc gained exactly one H6 bullet in the Hard-checks list per SS4.5, no other prose changed. This is dev-tooling (a Mix task), not an OTP process -- the idiomatic-gen_statem and supervision-isolation questions (docs/agents/reviewer.md items 1-2) do not apply to this diff; no anti-patterns.md entry is implicated. No type-safety gap worth filing: violation/grandfather shapes are plain maps/tuples consistent with the module's existing, unchanged convention, not a new pattern this diff introduces.
